---
title: "20 · A local model writes the specification"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

Notebook 19 writes a pipeline specification by hand. This one asks a model
running on your own machine to write it, checks what comes back, and runs it
through the same operator. The request goes to `localhost` and the endpoint
refuses any other host unless you say so, so nothing leaves the computer.

What earns the notebook its place is not that a model can produce JSON. It is
the three passes between the answer and the render: one strips what should
never come from a model, one applies rules a schema cannot express, and one
reports what validates but will still fail. The last example is a request the
notebook deliberately refuses to run, because the specification it produced is
valid and wrong.

The model is given the [pipeline skill](../guide/pipeline-schema.qmd), generated
from the same schema the executor reads, and a JSON schema passed as the
response format so it cannot invent field names.
